title: GPU oncall signal mapping and early-warning pagerflow
content:
Purpose
This is a working note for building an early-warning pagerflow for GPU node instability. Focus: signal mapping so oncall receives actionable alerts (and not noise) for ECC surges, NVLink negotiation glitches, driver hangs, and kernel panics.

Context and motivation
- We have recurring short ECC bursts that often precede more severe state (evictions, driver watchdogs). Oncall sees a flood of low-fidelity alerts and loses signal.
- NVLink handshake errors are intermittent and correlated with certain pcie link training outcomes; they sometimes cause soft kernel oops when combined with thermal variance.
- Goal: define alert tiers, recommended oncall actions, and simple automation to reduce pages for harmless transient noise while ensuring we surface growth patterns.

Observed signal types (examples)
1) ECC correctable spike (node-level)
   - Metric: telemetry.ecc.correctable.count (per-node, 1m)
   - Example pattern: 50->200 correctables across 1 minute, then decays.
   - Often seen with small driver resets or long tail of low-level dmesg WARN.
2) NVLink handshake failure
   - Observable in dmesg: "nvlink: link training failed, retrying"
   - Telemetry: nvlink.negotiation.retry.count and nvlink.link.up (boolean)
3) Driver watchdog (nvidia: GPU hung)
   - Kernel log: "NVRM: Xid \u003c3\u003e: GPU hang detected"
   - Side-effects: pod eviction, kubelet kill - sometimes triggers a host reboot depending on driver config
4) Kernel oops/panic with GPU stack present
   - Kernel oops text, stack traces referencing nvidia or amdgpu
5) Thermal excursions coincident with ECC spikes
   - hw.sensors.gpu_temp rolling above 85C with a rapid delta

Alert tiers and pagerflow (proposal)
- INFO/Slack-only (no page): transient single-bucket correctable increment < 10 in 1m and node never exceeds 30/min historical baseline. Post a slack message to #gpu-ops with sample context.
- WARNING (page to primary on-call via low-priority channel): sustained correctable rate > 100/min OR nvlink.retry > 10 within 5 minutes OR temperature > 88C with rising trend. This indicates a degradation that should be investigated but may be resolved.
- SEV (page + escalation): any driver watchdog (Xid >= 3 persistent), kernel panic with GPU stack, or repeated node reboots within 30 minutes. Immediate ephemeral mitigation required.

Example alert definitions (pseudo queries)
- ECC surge: sum(rate(telemetry_ecc_correctable_total{node="$node"}[1m])) by (node) > 100
- NVLink heartbeat loss: increase(nvlink_negotiation_retries_total{node="$node"}[5m]) > 10 AND nvlink_link_up{node="$node"} == 0
- Driver hang: count_over_time(kernel_log{message=~"GPU hang|NVRM: Xid"}[10m]) > 0

Runbook: first 10 minutes (primary oncall)
1) Gather context (commands):
   - kubectl get pods -A -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=$node
   - ssh $node (via bastion) or use fleet-ssh tool
   - sudo journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver -S "-15m" | tail -n 200
   - sudo dmesg | tail -n 300
   - nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,TEMPERATURE --format=csv
   - cat /proc/interrupts | grep -i nvidia
2) Quick triage checklist:
   - Are pods failing or evicted? If so, bouncing the node may be needed after containment.
   - Is NVLink link_up flapping? (check telemetry and dmesg). If yes, tag node for isolation and escalate.
   - Is temperature elevated? If above 90C and climbing, initiate thermal mitigation (slow down scheduler, move batch workloads).
3) Short-term mitigation (if SEV criteria met):
   - Cordon node: kubectl cordon $node
   - Drain non-critical pods with --ignore-daemonsets —grace-period=60
   - If driver is hung but kernel responsive: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver && monitor logs for 5 minutes
   - If kernel oops/panic or repeated reboots: file immediate hardware quarantine (mark node out-of-service) and trigger HW ops runbook
4) Evidence capture: attach /var/log/kernel.log excerpt, nvidia-smi logs, telemetry snapshot with timestamps, and link to Jira incident.

Lab repro and instrumentation attempts (notes)
- Tried to repro by injecting ECC noise via moderated thermal ramp in lab nodes with mixed PCIe risers; saw nvlink retry storms when one riser underclocks briefly.
- Repro steps used in lab (high-level): thermal chamber ramp 60->92C over 3 minutes + synthetic memory exercise (memtester) + forced PCIe repaint via echo
- Observed: nvlink retries increased after temp delta > 8C in 30s window. Not deterministic but reproducible in 2/5 runs.
- Actionable item: add telemetry histogram for temp_delta_30s and pcie_retrain_count.

Suggested automatic mitigations (short-term)
- Quarantine policy: if ECC surge > 200/min OR nvlink.retry > 50 in 10m, automatically cordon and schedule a maintenance job to capture logs and reboot driver. Use exponential backoff so flips don't thrash.
- Sampling change: increase kernel log capture window to 15m for nodes with WARNING alerts; keep full-verbosity for SEV nodes.
- Alert grouping: use node-level aggregate and suppress subsequent similar INFO alerts for 10 minutes to avoid alert storms.

Communication playbook (oncall -> infra -> hw team)
- Tag incident with JIRA-INC number and paste key artifacts to the incident page.
- If hardware suspicion: escalate to hw-ops with subject line: "Potential link/connector fault suspected: node $node - NVLINK retrain pattern" and include timestamps, dmesg snippets, and last known cabling changes.

Retrospective findings (recent wave, Feb 2026)
- 6 incidents across 2 weeks had NVLink+ECC combination, of which 4 resolved with driver restart and 2 required physical reseat of PCIe connectors.
- Root cause often multi-factor: slight thermal drift + aging backplane connectors + firmware handshake sensitivity.

Open action items (owners and rough ETA)
- Add temp_delta_30s telemetry and a pcie_retrain_count metric (Ethan Ruiz) — ETA 2026-03-20
- Prototype automatic quarantine job with exponential backoff (Daniel Cho) — ETA 2026-03-17
- Update oncall runbook with new alert thresholds and Slack templates (Priya Nair) — ETA 2026-03-12
- HW ops: schedule spot-check of connectors on problematic racks (Marta Silva) — ETA 2026-03-25

Notes and questions for follow-up
- Is the cost of extra sampling and log retention justified vs number of SEVs? lean towards short retention for WARN nodes, extended for SEV nodes only.
- Consider device firmware update window with low-traffic hours — requires coordination with platform engineering.

Appendix: quick commands cheat-sheet
- kube: kubectl get nodes -o wide; kubectl describe node $node
- logs: sudo journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -i nvlink
- driver: sudo systemctl status nvidia-driver; sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver
- nvidia-smi: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,memory.used,driver_version --format=csv

Revision log
- 2026-03-02: initial draft (Priya)
- 2026-03-05: added lab repro notes and quarantine idea (Ethan)
- 2026-03-10: updated thresholds and action owners (Daniel, Marta)

End of note.
